segment: Review of the published delta d323e2b..218059f: statuses per point, with the evidence that decides each one

environment_after_the_outage.live_gateway: hermes-gateway-1b7e7667.service active, pid 2627, served_profiles=[default, dest_telegram, telegram-bot-8812646969]; one receiver, no second
environment_after_the_outage.user_data: dest_telegram: 196 messages / 2 sessions, integrity_check ok; telegram-bot-8812646969: 4786 messages / 5 sessions, integrity_check ok; both WAL files are 0 bytes
environment_after_the_outage.unfinished_transactions: 19 intents without a committed record; 12 of them carry the product's own CONSUMED_NO_RETRY / SOURCE_UPDATE_CONSUMED_NO_RETRY state, 7 are closed qualification records
environment_after_the_outage.disk: /tmp is a 31 GB tmpfs with a 4 GB user quota; DSH's own temporary area is /home/jericho/.dsh/tmp on the disk; the project filesystem has 361 GB free

review_points.point: 1. the large copy that exhausted the quota
review_points.evidence: the apply-stage dry run copied the whole serving home into /tmp with shutil.copytree; the copy filled the tmpfs quota and every shell command then failed. The published v45 script also copied the entire hermes-agent tree (with environments and node_modules) inside v45_composition_checked_previous() and v45_composition_checked(); the 'generated' list in the code did not limit that copy.
review_points.action: the unbounded copies are gone. The new transaction never copies the runtime: the composition check runs over the live tree with the product's own proven_cache parameter, which proves the generated bytecode by digest instead of removing it. The isolated bench is built from the receipt's inventory only (17888 files, 257 MB) and lives in /home/jericho/.dsh/tmp.
review_points.verified: bench size 257 MB against 23 GB before; the bench run publishes 4 layers and 28+3 plugin files and completes with SOURCE_UPDATED_NOT_RUNTIME_ACCEPTED.

review_points.evidence: the session log shows the quota exhaustion and the owner's subsequent manual investigation; no kernel log or core dump was available to this session, so the causal link to the OOM and the VM panic is not established.
review_points.action: recorded as not proven; the dangerous copying pattern and the resource check are removed regardless, as the review requires.

review_points.point: 3. the v45 defects (two __main__ blocks, None constants, undefined source45 in update(), generator/validator mismatch, layer[1] indexing, O_EXCL re-creation, plugin_files update, final composition and rollback consistency)
review_points.evidence: the review explicitly allows replacing v45. The published friday_ordinary_v45_transaction.py keeps every one of those defects; fixing it in place would have been a 4300-line derivative.
review_points.action: the transition now runs through friday_v3_layer_publication.py: one entry point, no None constants, the schema flag is derived where it is used, the request generator and the validator agree field for field, the layer bodies are read as dictionaries, files are published through a rename instead of O_EXCL, the plugin set and the marker's plugin_files are updated together, and the composition check runs after the publication with a full rollback on refusal.
review_points.verified: full path proven on the isolated bench: request from the published generator, layers applied, product's own composition check passed, final receipt 180 -> 184 layers, and a controlled failure after publication restored every byte (0 changed files, receipt and marker identical to the original).

review_points.evidence: the v45 branch read the same candidate file for both sides of the comparison.
review_points.action: read_layers() reads the manifest and the patch bytes from the candidate tree and the preimages from the live home's receipt; the two are compared, never a file against itself.

review_points.evidence: prepare-worker-archive-request.py rewrites the product's failure record into a different refusal class, asserts 'A0: NOT_STARTED_NO_BOOTSTRAP_OR_PLAN' in closed-custody.json, and reconstructs the clock. The bootstrap state of the same attempt records a created container 3488cb15a180... with observed processes, so the A0 had actually started. Two copies exist with different digests (the archive-evidence copy: failure 394b88f2..., closed 45173d50...; the preparation copy: failure bb706ea7..., closed c632b8b5...).
review_points.action: both copies are marked withdrawn in place with a WITHDRAWN.json that names the reason and lists the digests; the files stay as artefacts of the failed attempt. The product's own failure, stop, native and plan receipts are untouched.
review_points.not_done: no new archive document was created in their place.
review_points.further_state: the product's archive engine never completed: the only archive transaction of the owner area holds stop-unconfirmed.json with state STOP_UNCONFIRMED. run-archive-engine.py supplies its own reduced verify() instead of the product's operator session, so its invocation is not equivalent to the ordinary operation and it is not reused as evidence.
review_points.live_a0_state: the current attempt e67597f05... is closed by the product itself (stop.json with STOP_CONFIRMED and retirement.json with INITIAL_PROBE_RETIRED). Two older attempts, 121b6c56... and a2039c22..., stopped in phase CREATE_UNKNOWN without a stop record; their processes no longer exist and the rootless docker daemon is inactive, so the stop happened but was never recorded. The daemon state directory and the route guard are absent, so the launcher-side retained-route precondition is clear.

review_points.point: 5. the data transfer and the repeated profile preparation
review_points.evidence: merge-preserved-user-data.py removes state.db-wal and state.db-shm before checking the target database, and reprepare-ordinary-areas.py deletes an existing archive before the next transfer. The serving home's two profiles currently show a 0-byte WAL and an intact database (integrity_check ok, 196 and 4786 messages), so no transfer is pending there.
review_points.action: pending: the scripts are not re-applied; the transfer path is rewritten with a consistent SQLite snapshot before it is used again.

review_points.point: 6. the product access reset and the advance_access contract
review_points.evidence: advance_access keeps tombstones and generations; the earlier reset wrote an empty users map with the schema key product_access.v1. The serving home's access store is intact and is not touched by the layer publication.
review_points.action: pending: the repeat preparation path, if it is needed, is implemented as a product transaction that keeps the access history.

review_points.point: 7. the reporting and the independence of the work
review_points.evidence: the owner chat is Russian and short by rule; the working memory is in the project materials; every substantive result is committed and pushed to the existing repository; no secrets, sessions or user data are placed in the repository.
review_points.rule_added: docs/WORKING-RULES.md now states that the chat language is Russian without exception, at the owner's request.
